classification.difficultyReason: Subtract the triple intersection from inclusive pair counts, complete the single-set and outside regions, then select regions for none, exactly one and exactly two.

content.prompt:
Use an appropriate Venn diagram.

In a group of 85 people, 33 own a microwave, 28 own a DVD player and 38 own a computer. In addition, 6 people own both a microwave and a DVD player, 9 own both a DVD player and a computer, 7 own both a computer and a microwave and 2 people own all three items. Draw a Venn diagram representing this information. If a person is chosen at random from the group, what is the probability that the person:

children.label: a
children.prompt: does not own a microwave, a computer or a DVD player?

answer.worked:
Let $M$, $D$ and $C$ represent microwave, DVD player and computer ownership. Put 2 in the triple intersection first. The regions belonging to exactly two sets contain $6-2=4$, $7-2=5$ and $9-2=7$.

The single-set regions contain $33-4-5-2=22$, $28-4-7-2=15$ and $38-5-7-2=24$.

$$\begin{align*}n(M\cup D\cup C)&=22+15+24+4+5+7+2\\n(M\cup D\cup C)&=79\\n(\text{none})&=85-79\\n(\text{none})&=6\\P(\text{none})&=\frac{6}{85}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: owns exactly one of the three items?

answer.worked:
The microwave-only, DVD-player-only and computer-only regions contain 22, 15 and 24 people respectively.

$$\begin{align*}n(\text{exactly one})&=22+15+24\\n(\text{exactly one})&=61\\P(\text{exactly one})&=\frac{61}{85}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: owns exactly two of the three items?

answer.short:
$\frac{16}{85}$

Exclude the triple intersection from each pairwise count.
answer.worked:
The regions belonging to exactly two sets contain $6-2=4$, $7-2=5$ and $9-2=7$ people.

$$\begin{align*}n(\text{exactly two})&=4+5+7\\n(\text{exactly two})&=16\\P(\text{exactly two})&=\frac{16}{85}\end{align*}$$
